title: BenchX work order
description: The runner's single input: what to run, against which target, how, and for whom. A runner executes one work order per invocation. See docs/design/work-order.md. The order carries only what its author decides; everything the runner can observe is captured by the runner, and comparison identity and series are never part of it.
$comment: Rules the schema cannot express and the runner enforces: target paths are absolute; the suite exists in target.build_dir; filter uses the harness's syntax; every listed quantity is one the adapter can map; a setting the runner cannot apply is rejected, not ignored. Shared types are references into urn:benchx:schema:measurement-result:0.1.0, which validators must load alongside this schema, so every value the runner copies into results is valid there by construction.

workorder_version.description: Work order contract version this object conforms to. Named differently from a result's schema_version so a loader can tell the two kinds apart.

project.description: Namespace for project-defined names and policy, copied to each result's project. Omit for an ad hoc run; its results are thin (result schema section 4.1).

source.description: Designated subject source whose revisions form the history axis, copied to each result's source.

target.description: The code to measure. Version 1 supports only an existing build directory; a revision to build and a prebuilt artifact need a new workorder_version.

build_dir.description: Absolute path of the build directory holding the suite. The runner captures the build configuration from it into coordinates.subject.configuration.

source_dir.description: Absolute path of the checkout the build was made from. The runner captures revision.key, provenance.subject_dirty, and provenance.subject_tree from it; if it cannot locate the checkout, subject_dirty is unknown and subject_tree is absent.

suite.description: Suite to execute; for Google Benchmark, the benchmark binary's name inside target.build_dir.

filter.description: Case filter in the harness's syntax, such as a Google Benchmark --benchmark_filter regular expression. Omit to run the whole suite.

quantities.description: Quantity names to emit. Each becomes coordinates.quantity.name of one result per case; results for one case from one invocation share an attempt_key. Units come from the adapter mapping.

repetitions.description: Requested observations per case. The runner records the request as comparison_context.protocol.repetitions {"mode": "fixed", "n_repeat": N} and the realized counts as procedure.attempted_repetitions and procedure.completed_repetitions. Omit to use the harness default, which the runner then records.

minimum_sample_seconds.description: Requested minimum duration of one observation, such as Google Benchmark --benchmark_min_time. Recorded as comparison_context.protocol.calibration {"mode": "adaptive", "minimum_sample_seconds": S}; the inner iteration count the harness chose goes to procedure.inner_iterations.

provenance.description: Who ordered the run and why. Nothing here enters comparison identity.

run_key.description: Grouping key assigned by the run author, who is this order's author. Copied to provenance.run_key of every result.

labels.description: Caller-supplied labels for selecting sides of a comparison, such as {"side": "baseline"}. Copied to provenance.labels.

requested_by.description: Person or system that requested the run. Result provenance has no field for it, so the runner records it as provenance.info.requested_by.

reason.description: Free-text reason for the run, recorded as provenance.info.reason.
